title: Clamp a loose right-angle pine joint with a trigger bar clamp
instruction: Clamp the two pine boards together at the corner, flush and square, with the trigger bar clamp, and let go of everything.
context: Clamping a joint is routine for carpenters (SOC 47-2031, over 700,000 US jobs, BLS) and anyone who builds a frame, drawer or box. A one-handed trigger bar clamp is made for it: one hand works the trigger, the other holds the work. Here a person has dry-fitted two pieces of pine at a frame corner, roughly: the stub is 8 mm short of flush with the rail's end and 2.5 degrees out of square. The clamp already hangs loose over the corner, its pads clear of both boards. The corner must be squared and flushed by hand and the trigger squeezed until the jaw bites, with the pads on the rail's back face and the stub's free end. Each full squeeze moves the jaw one 3 mm ratchet step and the pawl will not let it back, so 12 mm of slack takes four squeezes and two more load the joint. The release tab on the clamp's head must not be pressed. Then both hands come away and the corner stays flush and square.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of their midpoint, z up; arm bases at y +0.305 and -0.305 m. Positions in cm. Both arms start at their ready pose, grippers open. Nothing else is on the table. (1) Rail B (loose): a piece of 1x2 pine furring cut to 30 cm, actual 1.9 x 3.8 cm (3/4 x 1-1/2 in), lying flat, along y: x 22.5 to 26.3, y 0 to 30, mass 0.108 kg (est, pine 500 kg/m3), plain pine colour, friction on the bench 0.35 static (est). (2) Stub A (loose): the same pine cut to 10 cm, lying flat along x, 0.036 kg. It is a rough dry fit of the frame corner: its centre at x 31.7, y 2.7 and turned 2.5 degrees about the vertical, so its end face is 4 mm off B's front face (x 26.3), its outer face (y 0.8) is 8 mm short of flush with B's end face (y 0), and its far end is 4.4 mm off the square. (3) Clamp (loose): an IRWIN QUICK-GRIP Mini one-handed bar clamp, 6 in (about 150 mm opening, 2 in throat), lying on its side, 0.28 kg (est), yellow body and black pads and trigger: a steel bar 2.0 cm wide and 0.8 cm tall (x 21.0 to 45.8) with the fixed jaw at its left end (pad face x 22.2, 2.6 cm tall, pad 6.1 cm deep in y, 1.0 cm behind to 5.1 cm in front of the bar's centreline) and a moving jaw on the bar: pad face at x 37.2 with the clamp open (15 cm), a 6.2 cm head, a pistol grip with a handle 2.2 cm thick and 11 cm long behind the bar's centreline (x 39.2 to 41.4, the handle pointing away from the work, along -y) and a trigger lever 1.4 cm thick hinged at the head (x 44.2 to 45.6 at rest, 2.8 cm from the handle). Squeezing the trigger 1.8 cm toward the handle (about 4 N at the grip, est) pulls the jaw 3 mm (est) toward the fixed jaw: a ratchet, so the jaw never backs off; a small steel release tab on the head's far end (a 1 N m/rad return spring, about 9 N at its tip) frees the pawl if pressed past 60% of its turn while the trigger is not squeezed. The clamp starts hung loose over the corner: its bar's centreline at y -2.6 (the bar passes 1.6 cm outside the stub's flush outer face), the pads reaching y -3.6 to +2.5 (2.5 cm over the stub's width and the rail's), the fixed pad's face at x 22.2 (0.3 cm behind B's back face x 22.5), the moving pad's face at x 37.2 (0.9 cm beyond the stub's end once it is seated); 12 mm of jaw travel takes up the slack. (4) Bench stop (fixed): a strip of pine 1.9 x 2.0 cm, x 20.0 to 35.0, y -5.85 to -3.85, screwed to the bench 0.25 cm off the clamp's outer side (the jaw's and bar's faces at y -3.6); it touches neither board. No jig or corner block: the corner is held square by hand.
scoring: Read every control step from the poses of the stub, the rail and the clamp (its jaw position and trigger and release angles), the ratchet's pull and both grippers; the score is the last step's. Joint (measured in the rail's frame): gap = the stub's end face to the rail's front face; flush = the stub's outer face at the joint in from the rail's end face (either sign); square = the stub's far end off the perpendicular, in mm over its 100 mm. The stub must be on the rail's front side, both boards flat (under 3 degrees, tops within 3 mm). Tight: gap 1 mm, flush 1.5 mm, square 2.5 mm (1.4 degrees). Loose: 3, 3 and 5 mm. On the work: the fixed pad's face within 1.5 mm of the rail's back face, the moving pad's face within 1.5 mm of the stub's free end, both pads over at least 15 mm of the stub's width and of the rail's, the clamp flat (under 5 degrees) on the bench. Clamped: on the work and a clamp force of at least 40 N, the force being 20 N per mm of the ratchet's pull past the jaw's position, none if the release tab has turned past 60%. Hands off: on every step of the last 1 s both finger zones (a cylinder round the gripper's axis from the pad tips 38 mm up) are 30 mm or more from the stub, the rail and the clamp, unreadable arms counting as not. Still: over the last 1 s nothing moved over 1 mm or turned over 1 degree. Fell: latched, any part's lowest point more than 20 mm below the table top. First rule that holds sets the score: 0 if fell or not clamped; 0.25 clamped, joint outside the loose limits; 0.5 clamped, inside loose but outside tight; 0.75 clamped, tight, but a hand within 3 cm or something moved in the last 1 s; 1.0 clamped, tight, hands off, still. Possible scores 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held 1 s. A joint left unclamped, a clamp off the boards, a released pawl and a clamp that only just touches (under 40 N) all score 0. Real trial: gap and flush by feeler gauge and straightedge, square by a try square's blade (2.5 mm feeler over the stub's length), force by a one-off calibration of this clamp across a luggage scale (squeezes past contact needed for 40 N), then counted from video, a 30 mm spacer against each hand, video of the last 1 s.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. One declared rule, the ratchet: a squeeze past 80% of the trigger's travel steps the moving jaw's drive target 3 mm (est) toward the fixed jaw, once until the trigger is back under 30%; the drive is a 20 N/mm spring (est), 20 N per mm of pull past contact. The trigger stays a 4 N spring under load (real: its force rises). The release tab (past 60%, trigger not squeezed) resets the pull. Pine 500 kg/m3, friction 0.35; clamp 0.28 kg (est), boxes, rigid pads.
reset_notes: Lay rail B flat along y, its end face at y 0 and its back face at x 22.5 cm. Lay stub A flat, centre at x 31.7, y 2.7 cm, turned 2.5 degrees counter-clockwise (seen from above), 4 mm off the rail's face. Open the clamp fully (150 mm), lay it on its side, the bar's centreline at y -2.6 cm (over the corner, pads touching neither board, its outer side 2.5 mm off the bench stop strip, x 20 to 35, y -5.85 to -3.85 cm) and the fixed pad's face at x 22.2 cm. No glue is used in real trials. Nothing is consumed; re-check the stub's start position by a taped mark.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0; one arm (right only): 0.25; one arm (left only): 0.0
